title: NO MORE TEARS.
paragraphs: NO MORE TEARS.

Not someday maybe.
Not wishful thinking.
A promise.
But before that promise arrives, the Bible shows us something unsettling.
This world… is passing away.

The cities we build.
The graves we visit.
The tears we hide at night.
All of it.
Gone.
In Book of Revelation 21, the apostle John the Apostle sees a vision so breathtaking it almost feels impossible.

And yet it is Scripture.
And Scripture does not exaggerate.
Listen carefully.

“He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.”
— Revelation 21:4
Pause there.
Every tear.

Not just the visible ones.
The hidden ones too.

The tears you wiped before anyone noticed.
The tears you cried over betrayal.
Over regret.
Over the sins that still haunt your memory.
God sees them all.
And in the new creation—
He personally wipes them away.
But here is the tension most people miss.
Revelation 21 begins with a cosmic reset.

“Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.”
— Revelation 21:1
Not repaired.
Replaced.

The broken system of sin, death, decay—
the world infected since Book of Genesis 3—
will finally be undone.

No funerals.
No hospitals.
No addiction chains.
No secret shame.
Even the sea—the ancient biblical symbol of chaos and evil—
gone.
And then something even more shocking appears.
A city.
The New Jerusalem.
A holy city descending from heaven like a bride walking down the aisle.

Beautiful.
Radiant.
Prepared by God Himself.
And the voice from the throne declares:

“Look! God’s dwelling place is now among the people.”
— Revelation 21:3
Do you hear that?
Heaven is not just where we go.
It is where God comes to dwell with us forever.
No temple needed.
Because Jesus Himself is the center of everything.
But the chapter also whispers a warning.
This future belongs only to those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.
The Lamb is Jesus Christ.

The One who bled on the cross.
The One who carried our sin.
The One who rose from the grave.
The new world is not earned by good behavior.
It is entered by grace.
Grace received through repentance and faith in Jesus.
So let me speak to the person reading this quietly tonight.
You feel tired of this broken world.

The anxiety.
The guilt.
The endless cycle.
Listen.
The story does not end with tears.
The final chapter of the Bible is not disaster.
It is restoration.

A new sky.
A new earth.
A new beginning.
And the King Himself wiping the tears from your face.
Friend,

If you belong to Jesus,
your future is not darkness.
Your future is Revelation 21.

No graves.
No regret.
No more tears.
Only the presence of God.
Forever.
Because the world needs to hear this:
The end of the Bible is not destruction.
It is home.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
